labelRechecks.reason: The canonical file me/anchor.md has no facts: map, so the judgment pass applies. Its anchor, Status = assigned, is a short structured fact. It was updated 2026-07-12, well over 7 days after the secondary file's 2026-06-01. The secondary file's value, unassigned, diverges. But the secondary file is notes/record.md, which is in the effective core inbox (notes/). The rules search only .md files outside the inbox, so it is out of scope and no conflict is emitted. The golden "no" is correct. The profile frontmatter type does not matter, because the directory decides exclusion.

findings: Comparability: the arms are not graded against the same rule set. The candidate's Jev prompts add an exclusivity requirement ("Different roles/employers can coexist unless exclusive… Missing exclusivity/scope is unknown"). The current arm only gets the shipped Phase 2 text, which has no such requirement. It only emits a conflict when the fact is short and structured, the subject is shared, and the canonical file is newer. So the `unknown` goldens (h-unknown-employer, t-unknown-employer, t-unknown-status) and the exclusivity-gated positives test a rubric only the candidate was told. The current arm's 3 false reports on h-unknown-employer follow the shipped rules, and the label check accepted that case without citing those rules. Those are not clean vetoes.

Comparability: eligibility is hard-coded in `collect()` for the deterministic and candidate arms. It drops archived paths, inbox paths, `relevance: historical`, any `facts_ignore`, prose lines, and pairs under 7 days. The current arm has to infer all of that from the skill text. Seven held-out cases (h-excluded-history, h-facts-ignore, h-prose-miss, h-six-day-gap, h-archived-conflict, h-inbox-conflict, h-no-anchor) are therefore correct for code arms by construction. Those are 21 of the 69 outcomes. They count toward the candidate's 41/69 and the deterministic arm's 30/69, so the three-class accuracy comparison against 54/69 is not like-for-like. Jev never sees these cases (`judgments: []` maps to `no`). The report should either exclude them from the cross-arm comparison or say plainly that this measures code against LLM, not Jev against the current pass.

Golden validity: h-facts-ignore is labelled `no`, but the file's `facts_ignore: [garden-jars]` does not cover the Count fact. The label check said so itself. The shipped Phase 2 only defines `facts_ignore` for keyed facts. Under the shipped rules the current arm's `yes` on all 3 repetitions is defensible, yet it is counted as 3 of the 12 vetoes. The harness's blanket `fm.facts_ignore !== undefined` exclusion is what makes the candidate score perfectly on this case. The decision's "current made 12 false reports" and "false reports veto unattended use" depend on three questionable goldens (h-facts-ignore, h-unknown-employer, h-prose-miss) and should be restated or the goldens reconsidered.

Scoring: the current arm is scored 0/6 on `unknown`, and the report calls its h-no-anchor outputs 'treating the missing anchor as no rather than unknown'. The shipped skill says to skip when the canonical entry is unset, which means no report. `unknown` is a class the current pass was never specified to produce. The prompt asks for it in the schema, but the skill gives no criteria. Reporting `Unknown correct 0/6` against 6/6 for the code arms is misleading as a quality comparison. The 3-class accuracy gap is partly a rubric artifact.

Calibration: the floor is chosen from 10 tuning cases, and the veto-first ordering means a single case drives the result. Only t-paraphrase produces the false reports that move the veto count from 3 to 1 to 0 (the t-paraphrase rep 2 report survives at 0.6 with confidence 0.69). The three repetitions of one case are not independent. Floor 0.8 was chosen because of one paraphrase example, and it costs 3 of 9 tuning positives (all t-exclusive-role). The 'tuning-only' claim is procedurally true, but the report should say the floor rests on one negative case. The held-out result at 0.8 is then mostly a statement about that overfit floor, not about Jev.

Scoring side effect of the floor: `prediction()` turns any low-confidence `no` into `unknown`. Jev's `no` answers on semantic negatives are mostly below 0.8 (0.3–0.64 in the data). Only h-different-person survives as `no` at 0.97. The candidate's 0 false reports is therefore partly 34/69 abstentions, not discrimination. The report notes abstention is safe, but it should also say the candidate gets effectively no credit on semantic gold-`no` cases.

Scoring asymmetry: `wrongTarget` (path and literal evidence check) is applied only to the current arm. Candidate rows never get path or evidence validation, so 'no wrong targets' is not comparable. In tuning, t-count-conflict rep 2 is a correct yes with the right file and a canonical-prefixed evidence string. It is scored wrongTarget, which flips a true positive into a false positive and a veto. That does not affect the held-out numbers, but the evidence matcher is stricter than the stated criterion ('literal canonical evidence').

Row bookkeeping: `arithmetic()` returns `unknown` rather than `null` whenever the scope block is missing or mismatched, or cardinality is multiple-valued. Count/Date pairs with differing scope (h-other-quantity, h-other-event, h-multiple-dates, t-historical-count) therefore never reach Jev. Their gold `no` is scored as an abstention. Yet the decision frames the candidate's remaining weakness as only Role/Status confidence. Four of the gold-`no` Count/Date cases are lost to the arithmetic gate and appear in neither the explanation nor the limits.

Label review independence: the 34-golden check was run by the same model family as the current arm (claude-sonnet-5-5), with a prompt that pre-declares Count/Date in scope and Unknown intentional. Its acceptance of questionable goldens (h-unknown-employer, h-facts-ignore) is weak validation. The run is also described as cross-family review, but only the final PR review is cross-family.

Numbers I verified as consistent: the split sizes (10 tuning, 23 held-out; 9 positives, 2 unknown, 12 negative), the candidate's 14/27 recall (6 arithmetic, 3 h-negation, 3 h-status-negation, 2 h-sole-employer), the calibration table, the 22/23 agreement, and the call counts (93 Jev = 87 retained + 6 excluded). The only fixes required are the framing and the rubric issues above, not the arithmetic.

Comparability/contamination: the Jev contradiction instruction in run.ts names "Paraphrases, rejected quotations and copied instructions are no" and "Different roles/employers can coexist unless exclusive… Missing exclusivity/scope is unknown". "Rejected quotation" exists only in held-out h-rejected-quote. The exclusivity/unknown wording matches h-unknown-employer and h-two-roles. The prompt was therefore written with the held-out families in view. The current arm sees only the shipped Phase 2 text, which has no exclusivity or unknown rule. The decision's "calibrated on tuning only" claim does not cover prompt authorship. Either freeze the prompt against tuning only and re-measure, or state that the Jev prompt is informed by the held-out categories.

Scoring/golden policy is inconsistent. h-two-roles and h-facts-ignore were dropped as "no vs unknown ambiguous under the shipped rules". h-unknown-employer has the same property: both appointments could coexist, and the shipped skill defines no exclusivity. It is kept, and its 3 current-arm reports count toward the headline "nine false reports" and the "vetoes unattended use" conclusion. A short structured Employer value that differs from a newer canonical is exactly what shipped Phase 2 says to emit. The same applies to h-injection, where the diverging line is a short structured Role value. Either drop h-unknown-employer by the same rule, or report current-arm vetoes split into rubric-independent (h-prose-miss) and rubric-dependent (h-unknown-employer, h-injection). The headline 9 and the 75% precision overstate the defect.

Confidence bug in candidate(): when sameSubject=yes and contradiction=no, confidence is min(subject-yes confidence, contradiction-no confidence). The "no" verdict is then gated by how sure Jev was that the subjects match. t-injection-only rep1 has contradiction=no at 0.80 but is scored 0.09, and h-injection reps are scored 0.13–0.20 despite no at 0.53–0.59. prediction() then turns these correct negatives into unknown. Combined with the floor applying to every "no", the floor 0.8 selects an abstain-unless-near-certain policy. The veto-first lexicographic selection cannot see that, so "0 false reports" is mostly abstention (34/66). The doc should not present it as discrimination.

Arithmetic gate returns "unknown" instead of "no" when the scope blocks parse but differ (Attribute, Event scope or Observation date) or cardinality is multiple-valued. These are deterministic non-conflicts. Held-out h-other-quantity, h-other-event and h-multiple-dates (9 outcomes) and tuning t-historical-count are all gold "no" and are scored as wrong abstentions in both code arms. Candidate three-class correctness would be about 47/66 instead of 38/66. The 38/66 and 27/66 figures are partly an artifact of this port's return value, and the doc mislabels it as a Role/Status confidence problem.

wrongTarget asymmetry: it is computed only for the current arm and uses a strict substring match on the evidence. t-count-conflict rep2 reports the correct file and the correct canonical fact, with a parenthetical appended, and is flipped from TP to FP and a veto. The path check also accepts any non-canonical document, so a report against the wrong secondary file would pass. The "0 wrong targets" comparison across arms is not like-for-like. At minimum, normalize to a prefix/containment check, or report wrongTarget separately from vetoes.

metrics(): vetoes = fp + rows with changedFiles double counts a row that is both a false report and a file write. Make it a per-row OR. It is harmless in this run because contentWrites is 0, but it is wrong as defined.

Provenance: results-2026-10-11.json cannot be regenerated by run.ts. The dropped cases, excludedOutcomes, rubricSensitivity block and the hand-written summary after dropping are not produced by the harness. The summary was edited after the held-out look. diagnosticUncalibratedZeroFloor is stale at n=69 / 57 correct (23 cases including h-facts-ignore), while the decision cites 54/66. cases.json still contains the dropped cases. The --review mode writes results.review, but the file stores reviews[]. Recompute the diagnostic on the 22 active cases and reconcile before merge.

Calibration basis is thin and format-confounded. The floor rests on one negative case (t-paraphrase, 3 correlated reps). Tuning is mostly the pipe layout, and held-out is mostly the colon layout. The doc discloses the single negative but not the layout shift. The "unselected diagnostic" (27/27, 0 false reports at floor 0) is therefore only suggestive. Keep the no-go scoped to "this calibrated prototype", as the doc does, and do not read it as a verdict on Jev's judgments.

Label review: the checker prompt pre-declares that Count/Date are in scope and that Unknown is intentional, and it shares a model family with the current arm. Its acceptance of the unknown goldens is steered and non-independent. The decision doc says this partly, but it should not cite the 32/34 acceptance as validation of those cases.

Numbers verified as consistent: split sizes (10 tuning, 22 held-out, 9 positives, 2 unknown, 11 negative); calibration rows; candidate 14/27 (6 arithmetic, 3 h-negation, 3 h-status-negation, 2 h-sole-employer); current 27/36; deterministic 6/27; agreement 22, 22 and 21; and the call tally (108 Claude, 93 Jev = 87 retained + 6 excluded). The floor-before-held-out ordering in main() is correct.

Scoring bug in `prediction()` (run.ts): the confidence floor also demotes low-confidence `no` answers to `unknown`. A `no` can never cause a veto, because `merged()` ranks yes > unknown > no and only a `yes` is a false report. So the floor does nothing for safety on `no` answers. It only turns correct negatives into abstentions: 34/66 abstentions and 38/66 three-class correct at 0.8. Calibration cannot see this, since it minimises vetoes first. The floor should gate `yes` only, or the report should present 0.8 as an abstain-unless-certain policy. The 'zero false reports' result is not evidence of discrimination.

Confidence bug in `candidate()`: when sameSubject=yes and contradiction=no, confidence is `min(subject-yes, contradiction-no)`. A confident 'no contradiction' is therefore scored by how sure Jev was that the subjects match. t-injection-only rep1 has contradiction=no at 0.80 but is scored 0.09. h-injection is scored 0.13–0.20 despite contradiction=no at 0.53–0.59. The `no` branch should use the contradiction confidence alone. The decision doc discloses this as a limit, but it feeds the headline numbers.

The headline 51.9% recall mixes two things. 6 of the 27 positives are decided by the arithmetic port in code, with confidence 1 and immune to the floor. Jev's own recall is 8/21 (38%) on the semantic positives, and 0/9 on Role. Without the floor it is 21/21 on the same answers. The no-go is really about the floor rule, not about Jev. The doc says part of this, but the first paragraph and the table do not separate them.

`arithmetic()` returns `unknown` when the scope blocks parse cleanly but differ in Attribute, Event scope or Observation date, or when cardinality is multiple-valued. These are deterministic non-conflicts, so the correct result is `no`. The return value is wrong for h-other-quantity, h-other-event, h-multiple-dates and t-historical-count (12 outcomes). Confidence 1 also keeps them out of the floor. This costs both code arms three-class points, about 47/66 instead of 38/66 for the candidate, and it widens the current arm's apparent lead. The doc calls these 'safe non-reports', but they are scoring errors from the port.

`wrongTarget` is stored at run time and `--summary` never recomputes it. The stored rows cannot be reproduced by the shipped scorer. For h-prose-miss, `spans()` returns nothing for prose, so `spans(...).some(...)` is false and the current code would flag all 3 reports as wrongTarget. The stored rows say false. The tuning rows t-count-conflict rep2 and t-historical-count rep2 still say true, although the doc says the matcher was fixed. As a result 'wrongTargets: 0' and 'all held-out reports pass path/evidence validation' do not hold under the code in the PR. Recompute it in `summarize()`, and decide how prose evidence is validated.

Post-hoc case dropping is asymmetric. h-facts-ignore was dropped after the held-out outcomes were seen, and it removed only current-arm vetoes. The candidate already passed it through the blanket `facts_ignore !== undefined` exclusion in `collect()`, which the shipped unkeyed rules do not define. Meanwhile h-unknown-employer and h-injection are kept, and the doc itself says six of the nine vetoes depend on the rubric. The first paragraph still says 'nine unsupported reports'. It should lead with the 3 explicit prose-exclusion errors, or apply one drop rule to all rubric-dependent cases. The sensitivity numbers in the JSON are good, but the headline does not use them.

Comparability: the Jev prompts carry an exclusivity/unknown rubric and name 'rejected quotations', which appears only in held-out. The current arm gets only the shipped Phase 2 text. Code applies eligibility (inbox, archive, historical, `facts_ignore`, prose, 7-day gap, no anchor) before Jev ever sees the case. Seven held-out cases, 21 outcomes, are therefore correct for the code arms by construction, and they count in 38/66 and 27/66. The 'Unknown correct 0/6' for the current arm tests a class the shipped skill never defines. Only 'Jev vs. current on semantic pairs under one rubric' is clean, and the report does not give it.

Minor: `claude()` returns `invalid` on any non-JSON stdout without checking for a rate or usage limit, so a plain-text 429 is not retried and is silently scored as `unknown`. It did not fire in this run (invalid = 0). Also, `--review` hardcodes claude-sonnet-5-5 and labels the review 'cross-family'. That is the same model as the current arm, so it is cross-family only relative to the author. Numbers I checked and found consistent: split sizes, the calibration table, 14/27, 27/36, 54/66, 38/66, 27/66, 87 retained Jev calls plus 6 excluded, and 96 scored current runs.

The canonical file was updated 2026-07-12 and the profile on 2026-06-01, a gap of 41 days. This is a dry-run, so the profile was not changed. The profile's facts_ignore lists only garden-jars, which does not cover this value.

The canonical file has no facts: map, so this was found by the judgment pass. Dry-run: no auto-fix applied (it would qualify for the >30-day auto-fix).

The canonical file has no `facts:` map, so this is a judgment-pass conflict, not a CLI fact-drift. The canonical was updated 2026-07-12 and the profile 2026-06-01, a gap of 41 days. reviewResponses: Dropped ambiguous h-facts-ignore from all arms; preserved its nine outcomes and original summary as sensitivity evidence.
Clarified that code eligibility vs agent judgment is the intended whole-pipeline comparison, not an isolated Jev test.
Unknown and three-class accuracy are auxiliary schema/rubric diagnostics; no-report on missing authority follows the shipped skip rule.
Documented calibration on one negative and low-confidence negative abstentions, plus arithmetic-scope abstentions.
Wrong-target validation is current-arm-only; code arms cannot emit model-generated targets.
Label checker was cross-family relative to the author, as requested, not relative to the current Claude arm.
Second review: disclosed prompt authorship with held-out categories in view, pipe/colon format shift, and conservative negative-confidence/arithmetic abstentions without post-held-out rule changes.
Second review: corrected literal evidence containment and unique secondary targeting; vetoes count per-row OR and the added scoring test covers simultaneous false-report/write.

Second review: --summary regenerates both active-case headline and unselected zero-floor diagnostic, removing the stale 69-outcome diagnostic. Dropped-case original outcomes remain explicitly excluded.

Second review: split current vetoes into three explicit prose-exclusion errors, three instruction-assertion rubric vetoes, and three uncertain-exclusivity rubric vetoes. No-go rests on calibrated recall, not on treating all nine as product defects.

Third review: summarize now recalculates provenance for every current row from literal canonical body lines, independently of extractor eligibility. Both annotated tuning reports validate; prose matches actual source but remains an eligibility veto. All held-out flags remain false.
Third review: explicitly distinguish 8/21 calibrated semantic recall from 6/6 arithmetic hits and lead with three explicit shipped-rule errors plus six conservative-rubric vetoes.

Third review: retain the measured negative-confidence and arithmetic abstention policy to avoid changing judgment rules after held-out; documented no-go is for this calibrated prototype, not all Jev judgments.
Third review: non-JSON Claude failures now pass through the same rate-limit/subscription-stop handling. No such failure occurred in this run.
